verses.zh: 奉　神旨意，照着在基督耶稣里生命的应许，作基督耶稣使徒的保罗
verses.en: From Paul,[NOTE:1] an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, to further the promise[NOTE:2] of life in Christ Jesus,
notes: Grk “Paul.” The word “from” is not in the Greek text, but has been supplied to indicate the sender of the letter.
Grk “for the promise…” or possibly “in accordance with the promise…”
verses.commentary:
1:1 "Paul" Saul of Tarsus is first called Paul in Acts 13:9. It is probable that most Jews of the
diaspora had a Hebrew name (Saul) and a Greek name (Paul). If so, then Saul's parents gave him this name,
but why, then, does "Paul" suddenly appear in Acts 13? Possibly others began to call him by this name
he began to refer to himself by the term "little" or "least." The Greek name Paulos meant "little."
Several theories have been advanced about the origin of his Greek name:

- the second century tradition that Paul was short, fat, bald, bow-legged, bushy eye-browed, and
had protruding eyes, deriving from a non-canonical book from Thessalonika called Paul and Thekla,
is a possible source of the name

- Paul calls himself the "least of the saints" because he persecuted the Church (cf. Acts 9:1-2;
1 Cor. 15:9; Eph. 3:8; 1 Tim. 1:15)

Some have seen this "leastness" as the origin of the self-chosen title. However, in a book
like Galatians, where he emphasizes his independence from and equality with the Jerusalem Twelve, this
is somewhat unlikely (cf. 1 Cor. 15:10; 2 Cor. 11:5; 12:11).

▣ "an apostle" This came from the Greek word "send" (apostellō). Jesus chose
twelve men to be with Him in a special sense and called them "Apostles" (cf. Luke 6:13). This term was often
used of Jesus being sent from the Father (cf. Matt. 10:40; 15:24; Mark 9:37; Luke 9:48; John 4:34; 5:24,30,36,37,38;
6:29,38,39,40,57; 7:29; 8:42; 10:36; 11:42; 17:3, 8,18,21,23,25; 20:21). In Jewish sources, an "apostle" was someone
sent as an official representative of another, similar to "ambassador" (cf. 2 Cor. 5:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTLE

▣ "Christ" This is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew term messiah, which
meant "an anointed one." It implied "one called and equipped by God for a specific task." In the OT
three groups of leaders—priests, kings, and prophets—were anointed. Jesus fulfilled
all three of these anointed offices (cf. Heb. 1:2-3). He is the promised One who was to inaugurate the
new age of righteousness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

▣ "Jesus" This Aramaic name meant "YHWH saves," "YHWH is salvation,"or "YHWH brings
salvation." It is the same as the Hebrew name "Joshua." "Jesus" is derived from the word for salvation,
hosea, suffixed to the covenant name for God, "YHWH." It was the name communicated by God
through an angel to Mary (cf. Matt. 1:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "by the will of God" This same introductory phrase is used in 1 Cor. 1:1; 2 Cor. 1:1;
Eph. 1:1; and Col. 1:1. Paul was convinced that God had chosen him to be an Apostle. This special
sense of calling started at his Damascus road conversion (cf. Acts 9:1-22; 23:3-16; 26:9-18). Paul often
asserted his God-given authority and calling to affirm his writings as being uniquely from God
(i.e., inspired, cf. 2 Tim. 3:16; 1 Cor. 2:9-13; 1 Thess. 2:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WILL OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

▣

NASB, NKJV
"according to the promise of life"

NRSV
"for the sake of the promise of life"

TEV
"sent to proclaim the promised life"

NJB
"in accordance with his promise of life"

Peshitta
"by the promise of life"

Paul is asserting that his salvation, calling, and equipping for ministry are all
based on God's promises of real life, eternal life through Christ (cf. 2 Tim. 1:1,2,9,13). Paul alludes
to this concept of God's having and giving life several times in the Pastoral Letters (cf. 2 Tim. 1:1;
1 Tim. 6:15-16,19; Titus 1:2). God is the only source, giver, and sustainer of life.

verses.zh: 写信给我亲爱的儿子提摩太。愿恩惠、怜悯、平安从父　神和我们主基督耶稣归与你！
verses.en: to Timothy, my dear child. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord!
verses.commentary:
1:2 "to Timothy, my beloved son" This is imagery for Paul being Timothy's spiritual
father in the gospel (cf. 2 Tim. 2:1; Tim. 1:2; Titus 1:4). This opening paragraph shows their mutual
love.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TIMOTHY

▣ "Grace, mercy and peace" Notice the commonality and differences in Paul's opening greetings

- "Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ" (Rom. 1:7; 1 Cor. 1:3;
2 Cor. 1:2; Gal. 1:3; Eph. 1:2; Phil. 1:2; 1 Thess. 1:2; Philemon 1:3)

- "Grace to you and peace from God our Father" (Col. 1:2)

- "Grace to you and peace" (1 Thess. 1:1)

- "Grace, mercy and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord" (1 Tim. 1:2; 2 Tim. 1:2)

- "Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior" (Titus 1:4)

Notice that there is variety, but some elements are standard

- "Grace" begins all greetings. It is a Christianized form of the standard Greek opening. It focuses
on the character of God.

- "Peace" is the result of humans trusting in the trustworthy God, faithing His faithfulness.

- "Mercy" is another way of describing God's character and is unique to I and 2 Timothy. This term
was used in the Septuagint to translate the Hebrew term hesed (i.e., covenant love and loyalty).
God is gracious and trustworthy.

- The Father and Son are mentioned in each greeting (in 1 Thessalonians they are mentioned
in the previous phrase). They are always grammatically linked. This was one way the NT writers
asserted the full deity of Jesus of Nazareth. This is also true of the use of the OT titles for YHWH
applied to Jesus (i.e., Lord and Savior).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRACE, MERCY, AND PEACE IN PAUL

▣ "from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord" The opening phrase which follows
"grace, mercy and peace" has one PREPOSITION (apo) linking the Father and the
Son in an equal grammatical relationship (cf. 1 Tim. 1:2; Titus 1:4 and 2 Tim. 1:2). This was a grammatical
technique used by Paul to assert the Deity of Jesus.

"Father" is not used in the sense of sexual generation or chronological sequence, but
intimate family relationship. God chose family terms to reveal Himself to humanity (cf. Hosea 1; 2, where
God is shown as passionate, faithful lover, and Hosea 11:3-4,8-9 where He is shown as loving father and mother).

The Deity of revelation is not the Prime Mover or the First Cause of Greek philosophy,
but the Father of Christ Jesus. The Bible is not a human-reasoned philosophy but a divine self-disclosure,
a revelation which cannot be discovered by human analysis.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

▣ "Lord" God revealed His covenant name - YHWH - to Moses in
Exod. 3:14. It was from the Hebrew VERB "to be." The Jews were later afraid to
pronounce this holy name, when they read the Scriptures, lest they take it in vain and break one
of the Ten Commandments (cf. Exod. 20:7; Deut. 5:11). Therefore, they substituted another word,
Adon, which meant, "husband, owner, master, lord." This is the source of the English
translation of YHWH as Lord.

When the NT authors called Jesus "Lord" (kurios), they were asserting the
Deity of Jesus. This affirmation became the early church's baptismal formula, "Jesus is Lord"
(cf. Rom. 10:9-13; Phil. 2:6-11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (Adon and Kurios)

verses.zh: 我感谢　神，就是我接续祖先用清洁的良心所事奉的　神。祈祷的时候，不住的想念你，
verses.en: I am thankful to God, whom I have served with a clear conscience as my ancestors did,[NOTE:1] when I remember you in my prayers as I do constantly night and day.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “from my ancestors.”
Or “as I do constantly. By night and day I long to see you…”
verses.commentary:
1:3 "I thank God" It was typical of ancient Mediterranean letters to include a prayer of
thanksgiving at the beginning of the letter. Paul usually followed this pattern (cf. Rom. 1:8; 1 Cor. 1:4;
Eph. 1:15-16; Phil. 1:3-4; Col. 1:3-4; 1 Thess. 1:2; 2 Thess. 1:3; Philemon 4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THANKSGIVING

▣ "whom I serve. . .the way my forefathers did" Paul was not
conscious of Christianity being a separate or new faith from the OT (cf. Acts 24:14; 26:5-6,22; Romans 4;
2 Cor. 11:22; and Phil. 3:5). In Gal. 6:15-16 he uses the OT title "the Israel of God" to describe the church.
In Rom. 2:28-29 he asserts that the true children of Abraham are by faith, not ethnic descent (cf. Rom. 9:6).
There is no Jew or Greek (cf. Rom. 3:22; 1 Cor. 12:13; Gal. 3:28; Col. 3:11)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

▣ "clear conscience" See note at 1 Tim. 1:5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSCIENCE

▣ "remember" Paul remembers Timothy's life, family, and call to ministry. He uses
the term mneia in four ways in 2 Tim. 1:3-6.

- in 2 Tim. 1:3 Paul remembers Timothy constantly in his prayers

- in 2 Tim. 1:4 he uses the PARTICIPLE FORM to remind Timothy of their tearful separation

- in 2 Tim. 1:5 he uses a COMPOUND FORM (hupo + mneia) to
remind Timothy of his family's sincere faith

- in 2 Tim. 1:6 he uses a COMPOUND VERBAL FORMof the term (ana + mneia)
to remind Timothy of his calling and equipping for ministry

It is theologically helpful and encouraging to look back over our lives and see God's hand
which was involved at every stage (family faith, personal faith, call and equipping for ministry, and godly
friends and mentors).

verses.zh: 记念你的眼泪，昼夜切切地想要见你，好叫我满心快乐。
verses.en: As I remember your tears, I long to see you,[NOTE:1] so that I may be filled with joy.
notes: Grk “longing to see you, remembering your tears” (as a continuation of the preceding clause). Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
verses.commentary:
1:4 Paul and Timothy had a wonderful relationship in Christ's service. Their friendship
encouraged and strengthened them for ministry (cf. 2 Tim. 4:9,21).

verses.zh: 想到你心里无伪之信，这信是先在你外祖母罗以和你母亲友妮基心里的，我深信也在你的心里。
verses.en: I recall[NOTE:1] your sincere faith[NOTE:2] that was alive first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice, and I am sure[NOTE:3] is in you.
notes: Grk “recalling” (as a continuation of the preceding clause). Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Grk “the sincere faith in you.”
Or “convinced.”
verses.commentary:
1:5 "sincere faith" Literally this is "unhypocritical." It is used in the sense of "a pure faith" (cf. 1 Tim. 1:5).

▣ "within you" It is uncertain from the context (and 2 Tim. 3:15 as well as Acts 16:1)
whether this refers to Judaism (Timothy's grandmother and possibly mother) or Christianity
(Timothy's conversion). It obviously refers to faith in YHWH and His redemptive plan.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣

NASB
"I am sure that it is in you as well"

NKJV
"I am persuaded is in you also"

NRSV
"I am sure, lives in you"

TEV
"I am sure that you have it also"

NJB
"I am sure dwells also in you"

Peshitta
"I am sure now in you also"

This is a PERFECT PASSIVE INDICATIVE. This phrase in
Greek is a strong affirmation of continuing confidence in the Spirit's work in Timothy's life and
ministry (cf. Phil. 1:6).

verses.zh: 为此我提醒你，使你将　神藉我按手所给你的恩赐再如火挑旺起来。
verses.en: Because of this I remind you to rekindle God’s gift that you possess[NOTE:1] through the laying on of my hands.
notes: Grk “that is in you.”
verses.commentary:
1:6 "to kindle afresh" This is a PERFECT ACTIVE INDICATIVE which implies
an ongoing need to fan or rekindle or stir up the flame. There is the volitional aspect of giftedness. This
is not meant to imply that Timothy had let the flame of God's call and giftedness burn low, but that in
difficult situations like his current assignment, he should take strength from God's previous call and equipping.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "the gift of God" The root of the term "gift" (charisma), which is from "grace"
(charis). This could refer to the Holy Spirit or, better in this context, to his gifts of ministry. Every
believer has a supernatural gift or gift for ministry (1 Cor. 12:7,11,18). Timothy's gift was recognized by
Paul as well as his home church (cf. 1 Tim. 4:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRITUAL GIFTS

▣ "through the laying on of my hands" This cannot be a proof text for "apostolic
succession." See full note at 1 Tim. 4:14. Laying on of hands was used for several reasons in the Bible.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ORDINATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAYING ON OF HANDS

verses.zh: 因为　神赐给我们，不是胆怯的心，乃是刚强、仁爱、谨守的心。
verses.en: For God did not give us a Spirit[NOTE:1] of fear but of power and love and self-control.
notes: Or “a spirit,” denoting the human personality under the Spirit’s influence as in 1 Cor 4:21; Gal 6:1; 1 Pet 3:4. But the reference to the Holy Spirit at the end of this section (1:14) makes it likely that it begins this way also, so that the Holy Spirit is the referent.
verses.commentary:
1:7 "For God has not given us a spirit of" The most complete ancient Greek texts of the NT were written in
all capital letters (uncials), so capitalization in modern translations is a matter of interpretation. There
is no DEFINITE ARTICLE in the Greek text. There are also NT parallels for a small "s"
(cf. Rom. 8:15; 1 Cor. 2:12) yet in both contexts the Holy Spirit is specifically mentioned. Most modern
translations have "a spirit..." (i.e., KJV, ASV, NKJV, NASB, RSV, NRSV, NEB, REB and NIV). However,
others assume the Holy Spirit is being referred to here (cf. TEV, NJB and the William's translation of
the NT). In reality it could be purposeful ambiguity (cf. NEB and NJB).

God has given each believer the greatest gift, the Spirit, as well as a spiritual gift(s)
for ministry but also a bold and powerful desire to serve, to share, to go, to be Christlike.

Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the Old Testament, has an interesting
discussion of the uses of the term "spirit" in the NT (pp. 61-63).

- evil spirits

- the human spirit

- the Holy Spirit

- things that the Spirit produces in and through human spirits

- "not a spirit of slavery" vs. "a spirit of adoption," Rom. 8:15

- "a spirit of gentleness," 1 Cor. 4:21

- "a spirit of faith," 2 Cor. 4:13

- "a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him," Eph. 1:17

- "not a spirit of timidity" vs. "power, love and discipline," 2 Tim. 1:7

- "spirit of error" vs. "spirit of truth," 1 John 4:6

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE NT

▣

NASB, NJB
"a spirit of timidity"

NKJV, Peshitta
"a spirit of fear"

NRSV
"a spirit of cowardice"

TEV
"the Spirit. . .does not make us timid"

There are one negative and three positive aspects to the giftedness of God.

▣

NASB
"discipline"

NKJV
"sound mind"

NRSV
"self-discipline"

TEV, NJB
"self-control"

Peshitta
"good discipline"

See full note at 1 Tim. 3:2.

verses.zh: 你不要以给我们的主作见证为耻，也不要以我这为主被囚的为耻；总要按　神的能力，与我为福音同受苦难。
verses.en: So do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord[NOTE:1] or of me, a prisoner for his sake, but by[NOTE:2] God’s power accept your share of suffering[NOTE:3] for the gospel.
notes: Grk “the testimony of our Lord.”
Or “according to.”
Grk “suffer hardship together,” implying “join with me in suffering.”
verses.commentary:
1:8-14 This is one sentence in Greek.

1:8 "ashamed" This is a key phrase in this first chapter (cf. 2 Tim. 1:8,12,16; also note
Mark 8:38; Rom. 1:16). Here its grammatical form is an AORIST PASSIVE (deponent)
SUBJUNCTIVE; it does not imply that Timothy was ashamed, but is rather an
admonition not to start being ashamed.

Paul may have been alluding to the OT concept of sin bringing problems and
righteousness bringing blessings (cf. Deuteronomy 27-28; Job, Psalm 73). Paul was not suffering for
sin but for Christ.

▣ "of the testimony of our Lord, or of me His prisoner" Paul admonished Timothy to
continue to preach the sufferings of Christ (cf. Gen. 3:15; Psalm 22; Isaiah 53; Zechariah 11-14; Acts 3:18; 26:23)
and also to identify with Paul as a spiritual prisoner of the gospel and a physical prisoner because of the gospel!
Preach the good news regardless of the cost or consequences (cf. Gal. 4:17; 2 Cor. 4:7-12; 6:3-10; 11:23-29)!

▣ "join with me" Because of Paul's theology about the believers close
identification with Christ in death (cf. Rom. 6; Gal. 2:20) and suffering (cf. Rom. 8:17; 2 Cor. 1:5;
Phil. 3:10; also in 1 Pet. 4:13), Paul often forms new Greek words using the PREPOSITION
sun which means "joint participation in."

- suffer with (2 Tim. 1:8 and 2:3)

- died with (2 Tim. 2:11)

- live with (2 Tim. 2:11)

- reign with (2 Tim. 2:12)

▣ "in suffering for the gospel" This is an AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE
(cf. 2 Tim. 2:3, 9; 4:5; Rom. 8:17; 1 Pet. 3:14; 4:12-19). The key to this phrase is "for the gospel,"
not our own evil (cf. 1 Pet. 2:15-16). Modern Christians must recognize that suffering for the
gospel is the norm, not the exception (cf. Matt. 5:10-12; John 15:18-21; 16:1-2; 17:14; Acts 14:22;
Rom. 5:3-4; 2 Cor. 4:16-18; 6:4-10; 11:23-28; Phil. 1:29; 1 Thess. 3:3; 2 Tim. 3:12; James 1:2-4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO CHRISTIANS SUFFER?

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

verses.zh: 神救了我们，以圣召召我们，不是按我们的行为，乃是按他的旨意和恩典；这恩典是万古之先，在基督耶稣里赐给我们的，
verses.en: He is the one who saved us[NOTE:1] and called us with a holy calling, not based on[NOTE:2] our works but on his own purpose and grace, granted to us in Christ Jesus before time began,[NOTE:3]
notes: More literally, “who saved us,” as a description of God in v. 8. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Or “according to,” or “by.”
Grk “before eternal times.”
verses.commentary:
1:9 "who has saved us and called us" These are two AORIST ACTIVE PARTICIPLES
joined by "and" (kai). In Rom. 8:29-30 the "calling" comes before the "saving," referring to God's
sovereignty (election), but here the calling is referring to ministry (called with a calling, cf. 2 Tim. 1:6-8).

This is the NT equivalent to the covenant language of the OT used of Israel. Believers
in Jesus are the covenant people of God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (GREEK VERB TENSES)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

▣ "with a holy calling" This could refer to God as holy, but probably in context it
refers to God's will for a holy covenant people. God's will has always been for a people "made in
His image" (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) to reflect His image to the world (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6)! The work
of the Messiah has restored the image of God lost in the rebellion of Adam and Eve in Genesis 3. The
goal of Christianity is Christlikeness (cf. Rom. 8:29; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED

▣ "not according to our works" This was Paul's main preaching point to the Judaizers
of Acts 15 and the book of Galatians. The false teachers of the Pastoral Letters also have a Jewish
works-righteousness mentality which was based on the Mosaic Covenant (i.e., Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28;
30:15,19). This rejection of a works-righteousness is a recurrent theme in Paul's writings (cf. Rom. 3:20; 27-28;
4:4-5; 8; 9:11; Gal. 2:16; 3:11; Eph. 2:8-9; Phil. 3:9; 2 Tim. 1:9; Titus 3:5). The New Covenant (i.e., Jer. 31:31-34;
Ezek. 36:22-36) is a grace-based covenant.

▣ "according to His own purpose and grace" God's will and character cannot be separated.
He has acted on fallen mankind's behalf based on who He is (cf. Eph. 1:4-5, 11). The gospel reflects the
heart of the Father, the loving actions of the Son and the power of the Spirit. Salvation was God's idea,
God's initiation and God's provision!

▣ "which was granted us in Christ Jesus from all eternity" The gospel was not "plan B."
It was always God's plan to redeem fallen mankind, mankind made in His image and made for fellowship
with Him. As Genesis 3 records mankind's rebellion, it also records God's promise and plan
(cf. Gen. 3:15; Rom. 16:25-26; Eph. 2:11-3:13).

This predetermined plan through Christ is referred to often in the sermons of the
Apostles in Acts (cf. Acts 2:23; 3:18; 4:28; 13:29 as well as in Jesus' own words in Mark 10:45; Luke 22:20).
It is possibly alluded to in Titus 1:2 and Rev. 13:8.

Israel was only the first stage in God's plan of world redemption (cf. Gen. 12:3;
Exod. 19:5-6). The Messiah has always been the only hope for sinful humanity!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL

verses.zh: 但如今藉着我们救主基督耶稣的显现才表明出来了。他已经把死废去，藉着福音，将不能坏的生命彰显出来。
verses.en: but now made visible through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus. He[NOTE:1] has broken the power of death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel!
notes: Grk “having broken…and having brought…” (describing Christ). Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here (and at the beginning of v. 11) in the translation.
verses.commentary:
1:10 "the appearing of" The term epiphany here refers to Christ's first coming
(cf. 1 Tim. 6:14; Titus 2:11), but in 2 Tim. 4:1 and Titus 2:13 the same word refers to His Second Coming.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NT TERMS FOR CHRIST'S RETURN

▣ "our Savior Christ Jesus" Savior is an OT title for YHWH (cf. Ps. 106:21;
Isa. 43:3,11,15,21; 49:26; 60:16; 63:8; Hosea 13:4; Luke 1:47). In the NT it is attributed to Jesus as
God's Messiah (cf. Luke 2:11; John 4:42; 13:23; Eph. 5:23; Phil. 3:20; 1 John 4:14).

Only in the Pastoral Letters are both titles used in close proximity for both God
the Father and God the Son.

- God

- God our Savior (1 Tim. 1:1)

- God our savior (1 Tim. 2:3)

- the savior of all men (1 Tim. 4:10)

- God our savior (Titus 1:3)

- God our savior (Titus 2:10)

- God our savior (Titus 3:4)

- Christ

- our savior (2 Tim. 1:10)

- the Lord Jesus Christ our savior (Titus 1:4)

- our great God and Savior, Christ Jesus (Titus 2:13)

- Jesus Christ our savior (Titus 3:6)

- our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ (1 Peter 1:11)

- the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ (2 Peter 2:20)

- our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ (2 Peter 3:18)

The Pastoral Letters, written in the mid to late sixties, were also reacting
against the Roman Emperor's claims of being both God and savior (as well as these titles' use
in the Mystery Religions). For Christians these titles were reserved for YHWH and His Messiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR (title)

▣ "who abolished death" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: NULL AND VOID (KATARGEŌ)

▣ "brought life and immortality to light" The term "life" (zoā) is used several times
in the Pastoral Letters and can mean

- eternal life (1 Tim. 1:16; 6:12; Titus 1:2; 3:7)

- true life (1 Tim. 6:19)

- present life and life of the age to come (1 Tim. 4:8)

- promise of life in Christ (2 Tim. 1:1)

- life and immortality through Christ (2 Tim. 1:10)

There are two related terms used in the Pastoral Letters to express never ending, new age life:

- "corrupt" with an ALPHA PRIVATIVE (2 Tim. 1:10; Titus 2:7; Rom. 2:7; 1 Cor. 15:52-54)

- "death" with an ALPHA PRIVATIVE (1 Tim. 6:16 and 1 Cor. 15:53-54)

This is not the Greek concept of every human having an immortal pre-existing "soul."
Believers' immortality begins with their personal repentant faith in Christ. God is the only source of
immortality (cf. 1 Tim. 1:17; 6:16). He gives it freely through Christ (and Christ alone).

▣ "through the gospel" This Greek term originally meant "a reward for bringing
good news." It came to uniquely refer within Christianity to God's wonderful message of forgiveness
and acceptance through Jesus' life, teachings, death and resurrection. It later became the term used
to describe the books about Jesus' life (i.e., the four Gospels). Jesus is the good news of God's love
and provision for sinners.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOSPEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

verses.zh: 我为这福音奉派作传道的，作使徒，作师傅。
verses.en: For this gospel[NOTE:1] I was appointed a preacher and apostle and teacher.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “for which.”

Most mss (א2 C D F G Ψ 1241 1505 1739 1881 M al latt sy co) have ἐθνῶν (ethnōn, “of the Gentiles”) after “teacher” (διδάσκαλος [didaskalos ]). The shorter reading has poorer external credentials (א* A I 1175), though codex 33 has a reading apparently generated from διδάσκαλος alone (διάκονος (diakonos, “servant”]). The “teacher” without adjunct is preferred both because ἐθνῶν probably represents a gloss added by scribes familiar with 1 Tim 2:7 and because there is no easy explanation for the omission of ἐθνῶν if it were original here.
verses.commentary:
1:11 "for which I was appointed" This is AORIST PASSIVE INDICATIVE. In this
verse Paul is asserting his God-given gifts and tasks related to the gospel (cf. 1 Tim. 2:7).

▣ "a preacher" This is not so much a gift as it is a task (cf. TEV). Preaching is never
listed as a gift, but in a sense is a vital aspect of all the leadership gifts (cf. Eph. 4:11), which all
involve proclamation. This NOUN is from the VERB kērussō,
which meant to publicly announce or proclaim. It came to have a technical sense as a way of referring
to Apostolic preaching (kērygma) especially as it appears in the recorded sermons of Peter
and Paul in the book of Acts.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

▣ "an apostle" "Apostle" comes from one of the Greek words meaning "to send"
(apostellō). Jesus chose twelve of His disciples to be with Him in a special sense and
called them "Apostles" (cf. Luke 6:13). The VERB form is often used of Jesus being
sent from the Father (cf. Matt. 10:40; 15:24; Mark 9:37; Luke 9:48; John 4:34; 5:24,30,36,37,38;
6:29,38,39,40,57; 7:29; 8:42; 10:36; 11:42; 17:3,8,18,21,23,25; 20:21). In Jewish sources, the term was
used of someone sent as an official representative of another, similar to "ambassador."

This term had a special authoritative meaning. It was used of those who knew
Christ during His physical life and ministry (cf. Acts 1:21-26). Paul claimed that he also had seen the
Lord in his Damascus vision and call (cf. Acts 9). These men were uniquely called and equipped by the
Spirit to record and explain the events, teachings, and miracles of Jesus' earthly life.

The term came to be used of an ongoing gift in the church (cf. 1 Cor. 12:28; Eph. 4:11).
Their exact function is never specified; it may be church planting in new areas or regional leadership
(cf. Acts 14:4,14; 18:5; 1 Cor. 4:9; Gal. 1:19; Phil. 2:25; 1 Thess. 2:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTLE

▣ "a teacher" This is listed as a spiritual gift in Acts 13:1; Rom. 12:6-7; 1 Cor. 12:28;
and James 3. It is combined with the gift of pastor in Eph. 4:11 and 1 Tim. 3:2; 2 Tim. 2:24. When used
as a separate gift, it may refer to the training of new converts, but when linked to pastor it may refer
to the training of believers in doctrine (cf. 2 Tim. 2:15; 3:16-17).

The KJV and the NKJV have the added term "to the Gentiles." This does not occur
in the Greek uncial manuscript א* and A, but it does
occur in MSS אi2, C,
D, F, G, and other ancient texts. It does occur in 1 Tim. 2:7 and is probably an addition by early scribes.
The UBS4 gives its exclusion a "B" rating (almost certain).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

verses.zh: 为这缘故，我也受这些苦难。然而我不以为耻；因为知道我所信的是谁，也深信他能保全我所交付他的（或译：他所交托我的），直到那日。
verses.en: Because of this, in fact, I suffer as I do.[NOTE:1] But I am not ashamed because I know the one in whom my faith is set[NOTE:2] and I am convinced that he is able to protect what has been entrusted to me[NOTE:3] until that day.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “suffer these things.”
Or “in whom I have believed.”

What has been entrusted to me (Grk “my entrustment,” meaning either (1) “what I have entrusted to him” [his life, destiny, etc.] or (2) “what he has entrusted to me” [the truth of the gospel]). The parallel with v. 14 and use of similar words in the pastorals (1 Tim 6:20; 2 Tim 2:2) argue for the latter sense.
That day is a reference to the day when Paul would stand before Christ to give account for his service (cf. 2 Tim 1:18; 1 Cor 3:13; 2 Cor 5:9-10).
verses.commentary:
1:12 "for this reason I also suffer these things" This must relate to 2 Tim. 1:8. Paul knew
personally the price of spiritual leadership (cf. 2 Cor. 4:7-12; 6:3-10; 11:24-28).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO CHRISTIANS SUFFER?

▣ "but I am not ashamed" This refers to Paul's admonition to Timothy in 2 Tim. 1:8
and v.16. Paul's problems were in a sense evidence of his success in gospel proclamation (cf. Gal. 6:17)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

▣ "for I know whom" Notice that the emphasis is on personal relationship, not circumstances.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "I have believed" This is a PERFECT ACTIVE INDICATIVE which is literally
"I have believed and continue to believe." It refers to Paul's salvation experience on the road to Damascus (cf. Acts 9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, FAITH, OR TRUST

▣ "I am convinced" This is a PERFECT PASSIVE INDICATIVE. It refers to
Paul's confidence in God and from God, even amidst the persecution and imprisonments that he experienced.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ASSURANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRISTIAN ASSURANCE

▣ "He is able to guard" The phrase "He is able" is a wonderful descriptive designation
for God (cf. Rom. 16:25; Eph. 3:20 and Jude 1:24). God is not only able, but He is willing to protect our
profession of faith in Christ (cf. 1 Pet. 1:4-5) and our faithful lifestyle! Not only is salvation a God-initiated,
God-produced and God-consummated event, but so too, is the Christian life.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DESCRIPTIVE TITLES FOR GOD

▣ "what I have entrusted to Him" God guards believers' professions (cf. 1 Pet. 1:4-5). However,
believers must guard their stewardship of the gospel (see full note at 1 Tim. 1:18, cf. 1 Tim. 6:20; 2 Tim . 1:14).
Christianity is a covenant with benefits and privileges, but also with requirements and responsibilities!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "that day" This is an OT way of referring to the end time (cf. 2 Tim. 1:18). The OT clearly
revealed one climactic intervention of God into human history. However, from the progressive revelation
of the NT believers now know there are two comings, the incarnation (the inauguration of the kingdom of
God) and the Second Coming (the consummation of the kingdom of God).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

verses.zh: 你从我听的那纯正话语的规模，要用在基督耶稣里的信心和爱心，常常守着。
verses.en: Hold to the standard[NOTE:1] of sound words that you heard from me and do so with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “pattern.”

Grk “in faith and love in Christ Jesus.”sn With the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus. This describes the manner in which Timothy must hold to the standard (similar to Paul’s call for him to give attention to his life and his teaching in 1 Tim 4:11-16).
verses.commentary:
1:13

NASB
"Retain"

NKJV
"hold fast"

NRSV
"hold to"

TEV
"hold firmly to"

NJB
"keep"

Peshitta
"abide with you"

This is the very common "I have" (echō), but it has a wide
semantic range as the translations show. The form is a PERFECT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE.
Timothy must continue to hold on to the apostolic truth passed on to him by Paul (cf. 2 Tim. 1:14; Titus 1:9).

▣ "the standard" The term "standard" in Greek meant "to sketch" and was used of an
architect's designs (i.e., a blueprint). Paul had given Timothy the overall theological plan.

▣ "of sound words" This is a recurrent theme in the Pastoral Letters which refers
to healthy teachings (cf. 1 Tim. 1:10; 4:6; 6:3; 2 Tim. 1:13; 4:3,4; Titus 1:9,13; 2:1,2). This verse obviously
reflects the presence and problems caused by the false teachers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOUND TEACHING

▣ "in the faith and love" This refers to the manner in which leaders are to retain, pass on,
and defend the truth of the gospel (cf. 1 Corinthians 13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVE (agapē)

verses.zh: 从前所交托你的善道，你要靠着那住在我们里面的圣灵牢牢地守着。
verses.en: Protect that good thing[NOTE:1] entrusted to you, through the Holy Spirit who lives within us.
notes: That good thing (Grk “the good deposit”) refers to the truth of the gospel committed to Timothy (cf. 1 Tim 6:20).
verses.commentary:
1:14 "Guard through the Holy Spirit" This is an AORIST ACTIVE IMPERATIVE.
Note that believers must guard, but the Holy Spirit is the means and power by which it is done!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

▣ "who dwells in us" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE. There is
a fluidity between the work of the Spirit and the Son. G. Campbell Morgan said that the best name for
the Spirit is "the other Jesus" (cf. John 16:13-15). The following is an outline comparison of the work and titles of the
Son and Spirit:

- Spirit called "Spirit of Jesus" or similar expression (cf. Rom. 8:9; 1 Cor. 15:45; 2 Cor. 3:17;
Gal. 4:6; 1 Pet. 1:11).

- Both called by the same terms

- "Truth"

(1) Jesus (John 14:6)

(2) Spirit (John 14:17; 16:13)

- "Advocate"

(1) Jesus (1 John 2:1)

(2) Spirit (John 14:16; 16:7)

- Both indwell believers

- Jesus (Matt. 28:20; John 14:20,23; 15:4-5; Rom. 8:10; 2 Cor. 13:5; Gal. 2:20; Eph. 3:17; Col. 1:27)

- Spirit (John 14:16-17; Rom. 8:9,11; 1 Cor. 3:16; 6:19; 2 Tim. 1:14)

- Father (John 14:23; 2 Cor. 6:16)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS AND THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

▣

NASB
"the treasure which has been entrusted to you"

NKJV, Peshitta
"that good thing which was committed to you"

NRSV
"the good treasure entrusted to you"

TEV
"the good things that have been entrusted to you"

NJB
"that precious thing given in trust"

This refers to something entrusted to another for safe keeping. This is
possibly a word play on the term pistis, which is translated into English as belief, trust,
or faith. Believers have entrusted (see full note at 1 Tim. 1:18) their faith to God (cf. 2 Tim. 1:12).
God in turn has entrusted to them the gospel message (cf. 1 Tim. 6:20). Believers are stewards
of the gospel message. We will one day give an account to Him (cf. 2 Cor. 5:10) on how we have
handled this deposit of truth!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ORTHODOXY OF THE PASTORALS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE JUDGMENT SEAT OF CHRIST

verses.zh: 凡在亚细亚的人都离弃我，这是你知道的，其中有腓吉路和黑摩其尼。
verses.en: You know that everyone in the province of Asia[NOTE:1] deserted me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
notes: Grk “Asia”; in the NT this always refers to the Roman province of Asia. The Roman province of Asia made up about one-third of modern Asia Minor and was on the western side of it. Asia lay to the west of the region of Phrygia and Galatia. The words “the province of” are supplied to indicate to the modern reader that this does not refer to the continent of Asia.
verses.commentary:
1:15 "all who are in Asia" This is a hyperbole. Paul is emphasizing that most/many were afraid
and stopped associating with him.

▣ "turned away from me" Some of Paul's helpers (cf. 2 Tim. 4:10,16) deserted him
in his imprisonment (cf. 2 Tim. 1:8,16) but not necessarily deserted their faith in Christ. This was
probably related to Paul's Roman trial.

▣ "Phygelus and Hermogenes" Nothing is known about Phygelus or Hermogenes.

verses.zh: 愿主怜悯阿尼色弗一家的人；因他屡次使我畅快，不以我的锁链为耻，
verses.en: May the Lord grant mercy to the family of Onesiphorus because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my imprisonment.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “my chain.”
verses.commentary:
1:16-18 Verses 16-18 are an extended prayer (AORIST ACTIVE OPTATIVE).

1:16 "Onesiphorus" This is one believer and his family (or house church) who did not desert
Paul (cf. 2 Tim. 4:19). In unspecified ways (emotionally, financially) this man encouraged Paul while he
was in prison, as well as provided a needed ministry in Ephesus (cf. 2 Tim. 1:18).

verses.zh: 反倒在罗马的时候，殷勤地找我，并且找着了。
verses.en: But when he arrived in Rome,[NOTE:1] he eagerly searched for me and found me.
notes: For location see JP4-A1.

verses.zh: 愿主使他在那日得主的怜悯。他在以弗所怎样多多地服事我，是你明明知道的。
verses.en: May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day![NOTE:1] And you know very well all the ways he served me in Ephesus.[NOTE:2]
notes: That day is a reference to the day when Onesiphorus (v. 16) stands before Christ to give account for his service (cf. v. 12; 1 Cor 3:13; 2 Cor 5:9-10).
Grk “all the ways he served in Ephesus.”map For location see JP1-D2; JP2-D2; JP3-D2; JP4-D2.
verses.commentary:
1:18 "The Lord. . .the Lord" In Hebrew there is a clear distinction between YHWH
(Lord) and Adon (Lord, cf. Ps. 110:1). In Greek both are translated
as kurios. It seems that this prayer is addressed to the Messiah and refers to the "day of YHWH,"
an OT idiom for the end of time (a day of blessing or judgment).

This seems like a strange prayer to us. Some commentators have assumed
that Onesiphorus had died, if so this is the only prayer in the Bible on behalf of the dead. Paul was
asking that God bless his "house" (i.e., family or house church) because of his faithful ministry
(cf. Deut. 7:9; 5:10 and the same concept in 1 Cor. 7:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (Adon and Kurios)

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Did Paul see Christianity as separate from OT faith or an extension of it?

- What is the purpose of laying on of hands?

- List the theologically significant items in 2 Tim. 1:9.

- How has Jesus put an end to death?

- How is the word "guard" used differently in 2 Tim. 1:12 and 2 Tim. 1:14?

- Why did Paul's co-workers desert him? Does this imply that they were no longer believers?
